Flight Phase

Panneau de Contrôle des Modes

The autopilot interface panel allowing pilots to select, arm, or adjust flight modes such as heading, altitude, and vertical speed for aircraft automation.

Questions and answers

Questions and answers

What is Panneau de Contrôle des Modes?

In this glossary, Panneau de Contrôle des Modes refers to: The autopilot interface panel allowing pilots to select, arm, or adjust flight modes such as heading, altitude, and vertical speed for aircraft automation.

How is Panneau de Contrôle des Modes used in aviation?

In aviation communication, this term appears in contexts such as: "Officier: Cap et altitude réglés sur le Panneau de Contrôle des Modes ; pilote automatique armé. Commandant: Reçu, confirmez le mode approche armé quand établi."

Panneau de Contrôle des Modes matters because it supports clear communication in Flight Phase contexts for Pilots, Air Traffic Controllers, and Cabin Crew. It also connects to aviation training and exam language such as ICAO Level 4, ICAO Level 5, ICAO Level 6, and EASA FCL.055.

Where does this definition come from?

This definition is sourced from ICAO Doc 9432, FAA PCG and published by Protermify Aviation as a static aviation reference page.

Definition

The autopilot interface panel allowing pilots to select, arm, or adjust flight modes such as heading, altitude, and vertical speed for aircraft automation.

Operational example

First Officer: Heading and altitude set on Mode Control Panel; autopilot armed. Captain: Roger, confirm approach mode armed when established.

Localized term

Panneau de Contrôle des Modes

Localized example

Officier: Cap et altitude réglés sur le Panneau de Contrôle des Modes ; pilote automatique armé. Commandant: Reçu, confirmez le mode approche armé quand établi.
